==English==
{{was wotd|2008|December|24}}
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|lisen||obsolete}}
* {{alt|en|lis'en|lissen||eye dialect|rare}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:listenen<ety:inh<ang:hlysnan>>|tree=+}}
From {{inh|en|enm|listenen}}, {{m|enm|listnen}}, alteration (due to {{cog|enm|listen|t=to listen, give heed to}}) of {{inh|en|ang|hlysnan|t=to listen}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hlusnijaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*hlusnōną}} (compare {{cog|gmh|lüsenen}}), from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hlusēną}} (compare {{cog|goh|hlosēn}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱlew-|t=to hear}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sv|lyssna|t=to listen}}.

Compare {{cog|grc|κλαίω||to make known, famous}}, {{cog|cy|clywed||to hear}}, {{cog|la|clueō||to be famous}}, {{cog|lt|klausýti}}, {{cog|cu|слушати||to hear|sc=Cyrs}}, {{cog|sa|श्रोषति|tr=śróṣati||an exclamation used in making an offering with fire to the gods or departed spirits}} & {{cog|sa|श्लोक्य|tr=ślókya||voice, sound, noisy}}).

Related to {{m|en|loud}} and {{cog|de|lauschen}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈlɪsən/|[ˈlɪsən]|~|[ˈlɪsn̩]}}
** {{audio|en|en-uk-to listen.ogg|a=UK}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-listen.ogg|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|en-au-listen.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪsən|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|lis|ten}}

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L183}}
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|_|except in archaic usage}} To [[use]] one's sense of [[hearing]] and auditory cognition in an [[intentional]] way; to make deliberate use of one's [[ear]]s; to [[pay attention]] to or [[wait for]] a specific sound.
#: {{syn|en|heed|mind|note|pay attention|attend}}
#: {{ant|en|ignore}}
#: {{ux|en|Please '''listen''' carefully as I explain.}}
#: {{ux|en|I could hear you talking upstairs, but I didn’t really '''listen''' to your conversation.}} 
#* {{RQ:Weyman Chippinge Borough|I|01|passage=It was April 22, 1831, and a young man was walking down Whitehall in the direction of Parliament Street.{{nb...}}. He halted opposite the Privy Gardens, and, with his face turned skywards, '''listened''' until the sound of the Tower guns smote again on the ear and dispelled his doubts.}}
#* {{RQ:Grey Riders|4|passage=He reined Wrangle to a walk, halted now and then to '''listen''', and then proceeded cautiously with shifting and alert gaze.}}
#* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=1|passage=He read the letter aloud. Sophia '''listened''' with the studied air of one for whom, even in these days, a title possessed some surreptitious allurement.}}
#: {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}}
#:: {{ux|en|'''Listen''' the watchman’s cry upon the wall.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1485|author=Sir {{w|Thomas Malory}}|title=w:Le Morte d'Arthur|section=Book XX
|passage='But, sir, lyars ye have '''lystened''', and that hath caused grete debate betwyxte you and me.'}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-1|v|3|text=Lady, vouchsafe '''to listen''' what I say.}}
#* {{RQ:Thomson Summer|year=1768|passage=Here laid his Scrip, with wholesome Viands fill'd, / There, '''listening''' every Noise, his watchful Dog.}}
#: {{+obj|en|:to}}
#:: {{uxi|en|I like to '''listen''' to music.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|author=w:KT Tunstall|title=w:Saving My Face|album=w:Drastic Fantastic|year=2007|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3W4Elr3CnXE|text=I'm '''listening''' to what you say / Even though I look the other way / But you could never understand / The feeling of what I'm needing}}
#: {{+obj|en|:for}}
#:: {{uxi|en|You should '''listen''' for the starting gun.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[accept]] [[advice]] or [[obey]] instruction; to [[agree]] or [[assent]].
#: {{syn|en|mind}}
#: {{ant|en|disregard}}
#: {{uxi|en|'''Listen''', the only reason I yelled at you was because I was upset, OK?}}
#: {{uxi|en|Good children '''listen''' to their parents.}}
#* {{RQ:Orwell Animal Farm|1|passage=Never '''listen''' when they tell you that Man and the animals have a common interest{{nb...}}.}}

====Usage notes====
* In English, ''listen'' and ''hear'' are two primary verbs relating to audial perception. To {{m|en|hear}} most commonly represents [[automatic]], [[unconscious]], or [[passive]] perception of sound, while ''listen'' generally represents [[intentional]], [[conscious]], or [[purposeful]] use of the sense of hearing. The difference is expressed in the following quotation:

: As the silence took hold in the darkness, Sam realized that she had been '''hearing''', though not '''listening''' to, various low-level sounds—the hum of air conditioning and life support, the pulse of some faraway oxygen pump, the faint buzz of the electrical and lighting systems. —Justin Richards (1999) ''Demontage'', chapter 5, page 92.

* A similar distinction exists between ''see'' and ''watch'' in English.
